segments.arabic: [1189] حدثنا أبو معمر حدثنا عبد الوارث حدثنا أيوب عن حميد بن هلال عن أنس بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه قال:
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. Ayyub related to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: قال النبي ﷺ أخذ الراية زيد فأصيب ثم أخذها جعفر فأصيب ثم أخذها عبد الله بن رواحة فأصيب وإن عيني رسول الله ﷺ لتذرفان ثم أخذها خالد بن الوليد من غير إمرة ففتح له
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Zayd took the banner and was struck down. Then Ja‘far took it and was struck down. Then ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah took it and was struck down”—and the eyes of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, were indeed shedding tears—“then Khalid ibn al-Walid took it without being appointed to command, and victory was granted to him.”

checkedBody: Narrated Anas bin Malik:

The Prophet said, "Zaid took over the flag and was martyred. Then it was taken by Jafar who was martyred as well. Then 'Abdullah bin Rawaha took the flag but he too was martyred and at that time the eyes of Allah's Apostle were full of tears. Then Khalid bin Al-Walid took the flag without being nominated as a chief (before hand) and was blessed with victory."
comparisons.note: Renders أصيب as martyred and adds a beforehand explanation to the command appointment. Preserve the selected report’s wording and the narrator’s intervening tear description.

segments.english: Muhammad related to us. Abu Mu‘awiyah informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, from al-Sha‘bi, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: مات إنسان كان رسول الله ﷺ يعوده فمات بالليل فدفنوه ليلا فلما أصبح أخبروه، فقال: ما منعكم أن تعلموني قالوا كان الليل فكرهنا وكانت ظلمة أن نشق عليك فأتى قبره فصلى عليه
segments.english: A person whom the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to visit died. He died at night, and they buried him at night. In the morning they informed him. He said, “What prevented you from letting me know?” They said, “It was night—and dark—and we disliked causing you hardship.” So he went to his grave and prayed over him.

segments.arabic: [1191] حدثنا أبو معمر حدثنا عبد الوارث حدثنا عبد العزيز عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه قال: قال النبي ﷺ

segments.arabic: [1192] حدثنا مسلم حدثنا شعبة حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن الأصبهاني عن ذكوان عن أبي سعيد رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: Muslim related to us. Shu‘bah related to us. ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani related to us, from Dhakwan, from Abu Sa‘id, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

segments.arabic: أن النساء قلن للنبي ﷺ اجعل لنا يوما فوعظهن، وقال أيما امرأة مات لها ثلاثة من الولد كانوا لها حجابا من النار قالت امرأة واثنان قال واثنان،
segments.english: The women said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “Set aside a day for us.” He exhorted them and said, “Any woman whose three children die, they will be a barrier for her from the Fire.” A woman said, “And two?” He said, “And two.”

segments.arabic: وقال شريك عن ابن الأصبهاني حدثني أبو صالح عن أبي سعيد وأبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنهما عن النبي ﷺ قال: أبو هريرة لم يبلغوا الحنث
segments.english: Sharik said, from Ibn al-Asbahani: Abu Salih related to me, from Abu Sa‘id and Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Abu Hurayrah said: “They had not reached puberty.”

comparisons.note: The Sharik / Ibn al-Asbahani / Abu Salih closing route is abridged; preserve every named transmitter and the additional Abu Hurayrah wording.

checkedBody: Narrated Abu Sa'id:

The women requested the Prophet, "Please fix a day for us." So the Prophet preached to them and said, "A woman whose three children died would be screened from the Hell Fire by them," Hearing that, a woman asked, "If two died?" checkedBody: Narrated Um 'Atiyya

Aiyub said that Hafsa narrated to him a narration similar to that of Muhammad in which it was said that the bath was to be given for an odd number of times, and the numbers 3, 5 or 7 were mentioned. It was also said that they were to start with the right side and with the parts which were washed in ablution, and that Um 'Atiyya also mentioned, "We combed her hair and divided them in three braids."

segments.arabic: [1202] حدثنا أحمد حدثنا عبد الله بن وهب أخبرنا ابن جريج أن أيوب أخبره قال: سمعت ابن سيرين يقول
segments.english: Ahmad related to us. ‘Abdullah ibn Wahb related to us. Ibn Jurayj informed us that Ayyub informed him. He said: I heard Ibn Sirin say:

segments.arabic: جاءت أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها امرأة من الأنصار من اللاتي بايعن قدمت البصرة تبادر ابنا لها فلم تدركه فحدثتنا قالت
segments.english: Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, came—a woman of the Ansar, one of those who had pledged allegiance. She came to Basra, hastening to reach a son of hers, but she did not reach him. She related to us, saying:

segments.arabic: دخل علينا النبي ﷺ ونحن نغسل ابنته، فقال اغسلنها ثلاثا أو خمسا أو أكثر من ذلك إن رأيتن ذلك بماء وسدر واجعلن في الآخرة كافورا فإذا فرغتن فآذنني قالت فلما فرغنا ألقى إلينا حقوه، فقال أشعرنها إياه
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to us while we were washing his daughter. He said, “Wash her three or five times, or more than that if you see fit, with water and lote leaves. Put camphor in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” She said: When we had finished, he cast his waist-wrapper to us and said, “Place it next to her body.”

segments.arabic: ولم يزد على ذلك ولا أدري أي بناته وزعم أن الإشعار الففنها فيه وكذلك كان ابن سرين يأمر بالمرأة أن تشعر ولا تؤزر
segments.english: He did not add anything beyond that. I do not know which of his daughters it was. And he stated that ishar means: “Wrap her in it.” Likewise, Ibn Sirin used to instruct that a woman be wrapped in it, not have it tied around her waist.

comparisons.note: Replaces the central report with a reference to 1196; this is not a complete rendering of this occurrence. The arrival account says she hastened to reach a son and did not reach him, without explicitly saying that she could not find him. The final no-addition clause belongs to transmission discussion.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn Sirin:

Um 'Atiyya (an Ansari woman who gave the pledge of allegiance to the Prophet ) came to Basra to visit her son, but she could not find him. She narrated to us, "The Prophet came to us while we were giving bath to his (dead) daughter, he said: 'Wash her three times, five times or more, if you think it necessary, with water and Sidr, and last of all put camphor, and when you finish, notify me.' " Um 'Atiyya added, "After finishing, we informed him and he gave us his waist sheet and told us to shroud her in it and did not say more than that."
comparisons.note: Omits the closing uncertainty over which daughter, the explanation of ishar and Ibn Sirin’s concluding instruction. Adds a Prophetic designation after allegiance and a notification after finishing absent from the selected occurrence; the no-addition clause is not a further Prophetic statement.

notes: Keep the full embedded report, narrator uncertainty and concluding lexical/instructional material despite English abbreviations.

Keep the arrival and failure to reach her son visible outside the expandable chain. No identity of the daughter, Prophetic allegiance designation or post-washing notification is imported. Retain all final narrator remarks; the uncertainty is attributed to Ayyub by Ibn Hajar, and the ishar discussion is outside the Prophetic quotation.

The historical print names the Prophet and honorific after the allegiance clause; these are absent here from the selected and modern wording. Selected: «من اللاتي بايعن قدمت البصرة». brill-1862 (PDF 318): «من اللاتي بايعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قدمت البصرة». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 305): «من اللاتي بايعن قدمت البصرة».

The historical embedded report names the Messenger of Allah; selected and modern name the Prophet. This is separate from the previously recorded allegiance-clause difference. Selected: «دخل علينا النبي ﷺ». brill-1862 (PDF 318): «دخل علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 305): «دخل علينا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم».

segments.arabic: [1203] حدثنا قبيصة حدثنا سفيان عن هشام عن أم الهذيل عن أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Qabisah related to us. Sufyan related to us, from Hisham, from Umm al-Hudhayl, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: ضفرنا شعر بنت النبي ﷺ
segments.english: We braided the hair of the daughter of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

segments.arabic: تعني ثلاثة قرون،
segments.english: She means three braids.

segments.arabic: وقال وكيع قال سفيان ناصيتها وقرنيها
segments.english: Waki‘ said: Sufyan said: “Her forelock and her two side locks.”

comparisons.note: The selected she means explanation remains attributed, and the Waki/Sufyan closing gloss names the forelock and two side locks.

checkedBody: Narrated Um 'Atiyya:
We entwined the hair of the dead daughter of the Prophet into three braids. Waki said that Sufyan said, "One braid was entwined in front and the other two were entwined on the sides of the head."
comparisons.note: Turns the narrator’s she means explanation into the report and expands the compact forelock/two-side-locks gloss.

segments.arabic: [1204] حدثنا مسدد حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد عن هشام بن حسان قال: حدثتنا حفصة عن أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, who said: Hafsah related to us, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: توفيت إحدى بنات النبي ﷺ فأتانا النبي ﷺ، فقال اغسلنها بالسدر وترا ثلاثا أو خمسا أو أكثر من ذلك إن رأيتن ذلك واجعلن في الآخرة كافورا أو شيئا من كافور فإذا فرغتن فآذنني فلما فرغنا آذناه فألقى إلينا حقوه فضفرنا شعرها ثلاثة قرون وألقيناها خلفها
segments.english: One of the daughters of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to us and said, “Wash her with lote leaves an odd number of times—three or five, or more than that if you see fit. Put camphor—or some camphor—in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” When we had finished, we let him know. He cast his waist-wrapper to us. We braided her hair into three braids and placed them behind her.

comparisons.note: The first of two Prophetic honorifics is not retained in this English body; do not add an ishar instruction absent from the selected ending.

checkedBody: Narrated Um 'Atiyya:

One of the daughters of the Prophet expired and he came to us and said, "Wash her with Sidr (water) for odd number of times, i.e. three, five or more, if you think it necessary, and in the last, put camphor or (some camphor on her), and when you finish, notify me." So when we finished we informed him. He gave his waist-sheet to us (to shroud her). We entwined the hair (of the deceased girl) in three braids and made them fall at her back.
comparisons.note: Adds water and a shrouding parenthesis and collapses two Prophetic honorific positions.

notes: Both inspected prints contain the complete selected occurrence in sequence. Full chain, wording and honorific review remain required before any reader admission.
Preserve both Prophetic honorifics, odd count, camphor alternative, notification, cast verb and the three braids placed behind. No absent inner-wrapping command or water parenthesis is added.

segments.arabic: [1205] حدثنا محمد بن مقاتل أخبرنا عبد الله أخبرنا هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Muqatil related to us. ‘Abdullah informed us. Hisham ibn ‘Urwah informed us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ كفن في ثلاثة أثواب يمانية بيض سحولية من كرسف ليس فيهن قميص ولا عمامة

segments.arabic: [1206] حدثنا أبو النعمان حدثنا حماد عن أيوب عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهم قال
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, who said:

segments.arabic: بينما رجل واقف بعرفة إذ وقع عن راحلته فوقصته أو قال: فأوقصته قال النبي ﷺ اغسلوه بماء وسدر وكفنوه في ثوبين ولا تحنطوه ولا تخمروا رأسه فإنه يبعث يوم القيامة ملبيا
segments.english: While a man was standing at ‘Arafah, he fell from his mount and it broke his neck—or he said, caused his neck to break. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Wash him with water and lote leaves, and shroud him in two cloths. Do not apply burial perfume to him, and do not cover his head, for he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah.”

comparisons.note: Changes the prohibition on covering the head into a prohibition on shaving it. The selected Arabic and both inspected prints have the covering verb. Omits the narrator’s alternative waqasat/awqasat wording.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn Abbas:

While a man was riding (his Mount) in 'Arafat, he fell down from it (his Mount) and broke his neck (and died). The Prophet said, "Wash him with water and Sidr and shroud him in two pieces of cloth, and neither perfume him, nor cover his head, for he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection saying, 'Labbaik,' (i.e. like a pilgrim)."
comparisons.note: Changes the opening standing posture to riding and omits the narrator’s alternative wording. Supplies Labbaik and a pilgrim explanation instead of retaining the selected generic reciting-the-talbiyah expression.

notes: Both inspected prints contain the complete selected occurrence in sequence. Full chain, wording and honorific review remain required before any reader admission.

segments.arabic: [1207] حدثنا قتيبة حدثنا حماد عن أيوب عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Qutaybah related to us. Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: بينما رجل واقف مع رسول الله ﷺ بعرفة إذ وقع من راحلته فأقصعته أو قال: فأقعصته، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: اغسلوه بماء وسدر وكفنوه في ثوبين ولا تحنطوه ولا تخمروا رأسه فإن الله يبعثه يوم القيامة ملبيا
segments.english: While a man was standing with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at ‘Arafah, he fell from his mount and it crushed him—or he said, killed him on the spot. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Wash him with water and lote leaves, and shroud him in two cloths. Do not apply burial perfume to him, and do not cover his head, for Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah.”

comparisons.note: Changes the prohibition on covering the head into a prohibition on shaving it. The selected Arabic and both inspected prints have the covering verb. Omits the Aqsa/Qaas alternative and the explicit divine subject in the resurrection clause.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn Abbas:

While a man was at 'Arafat (for Hajj) with Allah's Apostle the fell down from his Mount and broke his neck (and died). So Allah's Apostle said, "Wash him with water and Sidr and shroud him in two pieces of cloth and neither perfume him nor cover his head, for Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection and he will be saying 'Labbaik."
comparisons.note: Omits the alternative verbs preserved in the Arabic. Supplies a Hajj parenthesis and Labbaik; preserve the source’s explicit standing and generic reciting-the-talbiyah wording.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Wash him with water and lote leaves, and shroud him in two cloths. Do not touch him with perfume, and do not cover his head, for Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah.”

A man was killed by his camel while we were with the Prophet and he was a Muhrim. So the Prophet said, "Wash him with water and Sidr and shroud him in two pieces of cloth and neither perfume him nor cover his head, for Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection and he will be saying 'Labbaik' . "
comparisons.note: Generalizes the explicit broken-neck verb to killed and replaces the generic talbiyah phrase with Labbaik.

segments.english: He died. He said, “Wash him with water and lote leaves, and shroud him in two cloths. Do not apply burial perfume to him, and do not cover his head, for he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection.”

segments.arabic: [1210] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد عن عبيد الله قال: حدثني نافع عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما
segments.english: Musaddad related to us; he said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who said: Nafi‘ related to me, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

segments.arabic: أن عبد الله بن أبي لما توفي جاء ابنه إلى النبي ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول الله أعطني قميصك أكفنه فيه وصل عليه واستغفر له فأعطاه النبي ﷺ قميصه، فقال آذني أصلي عليه فآذنه فلما أراد أن يصلي عليه جذبه عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه، فقال أليس الله نهاك أن تصلي على المنافقين، فقال: أنا بين خيرتين قال { استغفر لهم أو لا تستغفر لهم إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة فلن يغفر الله لهم } فصلى عليه فنزلت { ولا تصل على أحد منهم مات أبدا }
segments.english: When ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy died, his son came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “Messenger of Allah, give me your shirt so that I may shroud him in it, pray over him, and ask forgiveness for him.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave him his shirt and said, “Let me know, so that I may pray over him.” He let him know. When he was about to pray over him, ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, pulled him and said, “Has Allah not forbidden you to pray over the hypocrites?” He said, “I am between two choices. He said: ‘Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them.’” He prayed over him, and then it was revealed: “And never pray over any of them who dies.”

comparisons.note: Names Ibn Abbas as the narrator, whereas the selected Arabic and both prints name Ibn Umar.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn 'Umar:

When 'Abdullah bin Ubai (the chief of hypocrites) died, his son came to the Prophet and said, "O Allah's Apostle! Please give me your shirt to shroud him in it, offer his funeral prayer and ask for Allah's forgiveness for him." So Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) gave his shirt to him and said, "Inform me (When the funeral is ready) so that I may offer the funeral prayer." So, he informed him and when the Prophet intended to offer the funeral prayer, 'Umar took hold of his hand and said, "Has Allah not forbidden you to offer the funeral prayer for the hypocrites? The Prophet said, "I have been given the choice for Allah says: '(It does not avail) Whether you (O Muhammad) ask forgiveness for them (hypocrites), or do not ask for forgiveness for them. Even though you ask for their forgiveness seventy times, Allah will not forgive them. (9.80)" So the Prophet offered the funeral prayer and on that the revelation came: "And never (O Muhammad) pray (funeral prayer) for any of them (i.e. hypocrites) that dies." (9. 84)
comparisons.note: Supplies taking hold of his hand; the selected Arabic says Umar pulled him without specifying the hand. Parenthetical role/context explanations are not selected wording.

notes: Keep Ibn Umar as the selected chain’s narrator; the English web label names Ibn Abbas instead. The historical Quran excerpt extends beyond the selected and modern ending.

Keep Ibn Umar, both Prophetic honorifics, Umar’s honorific, the pulled-him action without a hand, and the selected Quran excerpt endings. No historical sequence reconciliation is inserted. Hemmed/unhemmed follows the inspected printed heading and classical lexical discussion; alternative readings stay outside the narration.

The historical address lacks يا رسول الله; the selected and modern occurrence retain it. Selected: «فقال: يا رسول الله أعطني قميصك». brill-1862 (PDF 320): «فقال أعطني قميصك». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 307): «فقال يا رسول الله أعطني قميصك».

segments.english: Malik ibn Isma‘il related to us: Ibn ‘Uyaynah related to us, from ‘Amr, who heard Jabir, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, say:

segments.arabic: أتى النبي ﷺ عبد الله بن أبي بعد ما دفن فأخرجه فنفث فيه من ريقه وألبسه قميصه
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy after he had been buried. He brought him out, blew lightly onto him with some of his saliva, and clothed him in his shirt.

comparisons.note: The active brought-him-out and explicit blowing with saliva are reduced; a second Prophetic honorific is supplied where absent in this occurrence.

checkedBody: Narrated Jabir:
The Prophet came to (the grave of) 'Abdullah bin Ubai after his body was buried. The body was brought out and then the Prophet put his saliva over the body and clothed it in his shirt.
comparisons.note: Retain the active brought-him-out action and explicit light blowing with saliva, rather than only putting saliva on him.

segments.arabic: [1212] حدثنا أبو نعيم حدثنا سفيان عن هشام عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us: Sufyan related to us, from Hisham, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: كفن النبي ﷺ في ثلاثة أثواب سحول كرسف ليس فيها قميص ولا عمامة
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was shrouded in three white cotton cloths. There was neither a shirt nor a turban among them.

comparisons.note: The Sahuli place adjective should not replace this occurrence’s bare plural suhul, white cloths, followed by kursuf, cotton.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Aisha:
The Prophet was shrouded in three pieces of cloth which were made of Suhul (a type of cotton), and neither a shirt nor a turban were used.
comparisons.note: Explains Suhul as a type of cotton; the selected سحول and كرسف need separate lexical treatment rather than merging the two expressions.

notes: The complete occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.

segments.arabic: [1215] حدثنا أحمد بن محمد المكي حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن سعد عن أبيه قال
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Makki related to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Sa‘d, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: أتي عبد الرحمن بن عوف رضى الله تعالى عنه يوما بطعامه، فقال قتل مصعب بن عمير وكان خيرا مني فلم يوجد له ما يكفن فيه إلا بردة وقتل حمزة أو رجل آخر خير مني فلم يوجد له ما يكفن فيه إلا بردة لقد خشيت أن يكون قد عجلت لنا طيباتنا في حياتنا الدنيا ثم جعل يبكي
segments.english: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, was brought his food one day. He said, “Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr was killed, and he was better than I. Nothing was found in which to shroud him except a burdah. Hamzah—or another man better than I—was killed, and nothing was found in which to shroud him except a burdah. I have indeed feared that our good things may have been hastened for us in our worldly life.” Then he began to weep.

comparisons.note: The selected closing word is good things, not good deeds. Retain our, the alternative another man and the repeated shrouding clause.

checkedBody: Narrated Sad from his father:

Once the meal of 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Auf was brought in front of him, and he said, "Mustab bin 'Umar was martyred and he was better than I, and he had nothing except his Burd (a black square narrow dress) to be shrouded in. Hamza or another person was martyred and he was also better than I and he had nothing to be shrouded in except his Burd. No doubt, I fear that the rewards of my deeds might have been given early in this world." Then he started weeping.
comparisons.note: The name Musab ibn Umayr is corrupted as Mustab bin Umar; explanatory garment parentheses are not source text. Retain killed rather than supplying martyred, and our good things rather than an explanation about my good deeds or their rewards.

notes: The historical main text lacks the Hamza-or-another-man clause retained by the selected and modern occurrence. Preserve the difference rather than harmonizing parallel reports.
Preserve Hamzah or another man, both complete shrouding clauses and our good things, distinct from the next occurrence’s good deeds.

The historical main text omits the Hamza-or-another-man clause; selected and modern retain this separately repeated statement. Selected: «فلم يوجد له ما يكفن فيه إلا بردة وقتل حمزة أو رجل آخر خير مني فلم يوجد له ما يكفن فيه إلا بردة». brill-1862 (PDF 321): «فلم يوجد له ما يكفن فيه إلا بردة لقد خشيت». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 308): «فلم يوجد له ما يكفن فيه إلا بردة وقتل حمزة أو رجل آخر خير مني فلم يوجد له ما يكفن فيه إلا بردة لقد خشيت».

segments.arabic: [1216] حدثنا ابن مقاتل أخبرنا عبد الله أخبرنا شعبة عن سعد بن إبراهيم عن أبيه إبراهيم
segments.english: Ibn Muqatil related to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Shu‘bah informed us, from Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim, from his father Ibrahim:

segments.arabic: أن عبد الرحمن بن عوف رضى الله تعالى عنه أتى بطعام وكان صائما، فقال قتل مصعب بن عمير وهو خير مني كفن في بردة إن غطي رأسه بدت رجلاه وإن غطي رجلاه بدا رأسه
segments.english: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, was brought food while he was fasting. He said, “Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr was killed, and he was better than I. He was shrouded in a burdah: if his head was covered, his feet showed, and if his feet were covered, his head showed.”

segments.arabic: وأراه قال
segments.english: And I think he said:

segments.arabic: وقتل حمزة وهو خير مني ثم بسط لنا من الدنيا ما بسط
segments.english: “And Hamzah was killed, and he was better than I. Then this world was opened up to us as it was opened up”—

segments.arabic: أو قال
segments.english: Or he said:

segments.arabic: أعطينا من الدنيا ما أعطينا وقد خشينا أن تكون حسناتنا عجلت لنا ثم جعل يبكي حتى ترك الطعام
segments.english: “We were given of this world what we were given. And we have feared that our good deeds have been hastened for us.” Then he began to weep until he left the food.

comparisons.note: Renders the narrator uncertainty as seeing him speak, adds the other-man alternative absent from this occurrence, and truncates the sentence about good deeds being advanced.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibrahim:

Once a meal was brought to 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Auf and he was fasting. He said, "Mustab bin 'Umar was martyred and he was better than I and was shrouded in his Burd and when his head was covered with it, his legs became bare, and when his legs were covered his head got uncovered. Hamza was martyred and was better than I. Now the worldly wealth have been bestowed upon us (or said a similar thing). No doubt, I fear that the rewards of my deeds might have been given earlier in this world." Then he started weeping and left his food.
comparisons.note: Corrupts the name Musab ibn Umayr, drops the narrator’s uncertainty before the Hamza clause, and abridges the expressly quoted alternative.

notes: Keep the narrator uncertainty, both quoted alternatives and the full ending despite abbreviations in the English comparisons.

Keep Ibn Muqatil unexpanded, the repeated father’s name Ibrahim, both covering clauses, both narrator asides and both complete worldly-provision alternatives. No other-man alternative or truncated closing fear is imported.

Both prints give Muhammad ibn Muqatil; the selected first name is absent. Selected: «حدثنا ابن مقاتل». brill-1862 (PDF 321): «حدثنا محمد بن مقاتل». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 308): «حدثنا محمد بن مقاتل».

segments.arabic: [1217] حدثنا عمر بن حفص بن غياث حدثنا أبي حدثنا الأعمش حدثنا شقيق حدثنا خباب رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: ‘Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us: My father related to us: Al-A‘mash related to us: Shaqiq related to us: Khabbab, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, related to us; he said:

segments.arabic: هاجرنا مع النبي ﷺ نلتمس وجه الله فوقع أجرنا على الله فمنا من مات لم يأكل من أجره شيئا منهم مصعب بن عمير ومنا من أينعت له ثمرته فهو يهدبها قتل يوم أحد فلم نجد ما نكفنه إلا بردة إذا غطينا بها رأسه خرجت رجلاه وإذا غطينا رجليه خرج رأسه فأمرنا النبي ﷺ أن نغطي رأسه وأن نجعل على رجليه من الإذخر
segments.english: We emigrated with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, seeking the Face of Allah, so our reward became due from Allah. Some of us died without eating anything of their reward; among them was Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr. And among us is one whose fruit has ripened, and he is plucking it. He was killed on the day of Uhud, and we found nothing in which to shroud him except a burdah. When we covered his head with it, his feet showed, and when we covered his feet, his head showed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to cover his head and to put some idhkhir on his feet.

comparisons.note: Retain the selected Face of Allah wording and the complete fruit-ripening/plucking image without replacing them with interpretive equivalents.

checkedBody: Narrated Khabbab:

We emigrated with the Prophet (p.b.u.h) in Allah's cause, and so our reward was then surely incumbent on Allah. Some of us died and they did not take anything from their rewards in this world, and amongst them was Mustab bin 'Umar; and the others were those who got their rewards. Mustab bin 'Umar was martyred on the day of the Battle of Uhud and we could get nothing except his Burd to shroud him in. And when we covered his head his feet became bare and vice versa. So the Prophet ordered us to cover his head only and to put idhkhir (a kind of shrub) over his feet.
comparisons.note: Corrupts Musab ibn Umayr and replaces the fruit-ripening/plucking image with an explanatory statement about rewards. Keep Face of Allah and both complete head/feet covering clauses rather than an explanatory rendering and vice versa.

notes: The complete occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.
Keep Face of Allah, the reward expression, the complete fruit image, the source’s order, both covering clauses and idhkhir without a supplied botanical identification.

segments.arabic: [1218] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة حدثنا ابن أبي حازم عن أبيه عن سهل رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us: Ibn Abi Hazim related to us, from his father, from Sahl, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

segments.arabic: أن امرأة جاءت النبي ﷺ ببردة منسوجة فيها حاشيتها
segments.english: A woman came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with a woven burdah with its border.

segments.arabic: أتدرون ما البردة قالوا الشملة قال: نعم
segments.english: “Do you know what a burdah is?” They said, “A wrap.” He said, “Yes.”

segments.arabic: قالت نسجتها بيدي فجئت لأكسوكها فأخذها النبي ﷺ محتاجا إليها فخرج إلينا وإنها إزاره فحسنها فلان، فقال اكسنيها ما أحسنها قال القوم ما أحسنت لبسها النبي ﷺ محتاجا إليها ثم سألته وعلمت أنه لا يرد قال إني والله ما سألته لألبسها إنما سألته لتكون كفني
segments.english: She said, “I wove it with my hand and have come to clothe you in it.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took it, being in need of it. He came out to us wearing it as his waist-wrapper. So-and-so admired it and said, “Clothe me in it. How beautiful it is!” The people said, “You have not done well. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wore it because he needed it, and then you asked him for it, knowing that he does not refuse.” He said, “By Allah, I did not ask him for it to wear it. I only asked him for it so that it would be my shroud.”

segments.arabic: قال سهل فكانت كفنه
segments.english: Sahl said: It became his shroud.

comparisons.note: The selected with-my-hand is singular, and the definition dialogue remains a transmission aside separate from the woman’s words.

checkedBody: Narrated Sahl:

A woman brought a woven Burda (sheet) having edging (border) to the Prophet, Then Sahl asked them whether they knew what is Burda, they said that Burda is a cloak and Sahl confirmed their reply. Then the woman said, "I have woven it with my own hands and I have brought it so that you may wear it." The Prophet accepted it, and at that time he was in need of it. So he came out wearing it as his waist-sheet. A man praised it and said, "Will you give it to me? How nice it is!" The other people said, "You have not done the right thing as the Prophet is in need of it and you have asked for it when you know that he never turns down anybody's request." The man replied, "By Allah, I have not asked for it to wear it but to make it my shroud." Later it was his shroud.
comparisons.note: Does not preserve the explicit final Sahl attribution; keep the embedded definition exchange separate from the woman’s words. The selected with-my-hand is singular. Do not supply a speaker name inside the definition dialogue where the selected Arabic does not explicitly name one.

segments.arabic: [1219] حدثنا قبيصة بن عقبة حدثنا سفيان عن خالد عن أم الهذيل عن أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Qabisah ibn ‘Uqbah related to us: Sufyan related to us, from Khalid, from Umm al-Hudhayl, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: نهينا عن اتباع الجنائز ولم يعزم علينا
segments.english: We were forbidden to follow funeral processions, but it was not firmly imposed on us.

notes: The complete occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.

segments.arabic: [1220] حدثنا مسدد حدثنا بشر بن المفضل حدثنا سلمة بن علقمة عن محمد بن سيرين قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us: Salamah ibn ‘Alqamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said:

segments.arabic: توفي بن لأم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها فلما كان اليوم الثالث دعت بصفرة فتمسحت به وقالت نهينا أن نحد أكثر من ثلاث إلا بزوج
segments.english: A son of Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, died. On the third day she called for yellow perfume and rubbed herself with it. She said, “We were forbidden to observe mourning for more than three days, except for a husband.”

notes: The complete occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.
Safrah is yellow perfume in this context. Formal mourning, the third day, rubbing and the husband exception remain; this is source wording, not additional legal advice.
The historical pronoun is feminine; selected and modern have the masculine form. Selected: «فتمسحت به». brill-1862 (PDF 322): «فتمسحت بها». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 309): «فتمسحت به».

segments.arabic: [1221] حدثنا الحميدي حدثنا سفيان حدثنا أيوب بن موسى قال: أخبرني حميد بن نافع عن زينب بنت أبي سلمة قالت
segments.english: Al-Humaydi related to us: Sufyan related to us: Ayyub ibn Musa related to us; he said: Humayd ibn Nafi‘ informed me, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, who said:

segments.arabic: لما جاء نعي أبي سفيان من الشام دعت أم حبيبة رضى الله تعالى عنها بصفرة في اليوم الثالث فمسحت عارضيها وذراعيها وقالت إني كنت عن هذا لغنية لولا أني سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: لا يحل لامرأة تؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر أن تحد على ميت فوق ثلاث إلا على زوج فإنها تحد عليه أربعة أشهر وعشرا
segments.english: When news of Abu Sufyan’s death came from al-Sham, Umm Habibah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, called for yellow perfume on the third day and rubbed her cheeks and forearms with it. She said, “I would have had no need of this, had I not heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to observe mourning for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband, for whom she observes mourning for four months and ten days.’”

notes: The complete occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.

segments.arabic: [1222] حدثنا إسماعيل حدثني مالك عن عبد الله بن أبي بكر ابن محمد بن عمرو بن حزم عن حميد بن نافع عن زينب بنت أبي سلمة أخبرته قالت
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us: Malik related to me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm, from Humayd ibn Nafi‘, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, who informed him; she said:

segments.arabic: دخلت على أم حبيبة زوج النبي ﷺ فقالت سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: لا يحل لامرأة تؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر تحد على ميت فوق ثلاث إلا على زوج أربعة أشهر وعشرا
segments.english: I visited Umm Habibah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. She said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to observe mourning for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband: four months and ten days.’”

segments.arabic: ثم دخلت على زينب بنت جحش حين توفي أخوها فدعت بطيب فمست، ثم قالت ما لي بالطيب من حاجة غير أني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ على المنبر لا يحل لامرأة تؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر تحد على ميت فوق ثلاث إلا على زوج أربعة أشهر وعشرا
segments.english: Then I visited Zaynab bint Jahsh when her brother died. She called for perfume and applied it. Then she said, “I have no need of perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the pulpit: ‘It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to observe mourning for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband: four months and ten days.’”

comparisons.note: The first Prophetic honorific is not retained. Preserve I have no need of perfume rather than recasting it as I only put on perfume, and retain both complete quoted statements.

checkedBody: Narrated Zainab bint Abi Salama :

I went to Um Habiba, the wife of Prophet, who said, "I heard the Prophets saying, 'It is not legal for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for any dead person for more than three days except for her husband, (for whom she should mourn) for four months and ten days'." Later I went to Zainab bint Jahsh when her brother died; she asked for some scent, and after using it she said, "I am not in need of scent but I heard Allah's Apostle saying, 'It is not legal for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for more than three days for any dead person except her husband, (for whom she should mourn) for four months and ten days.' "
comparisons.note: Omits the minbar location in the second account. Both repeated statements and the second visit must remain complete.

notes: One digital entry includes two separately numbered modern printed accounts, 1281/1282. Both visits and repeated statements belong to this selected occurrence.

The selected complete occurrence spans modern 1281/1282. Preserve the full long chain, who informed him, both visits, both identical statements, the pulpit and all three honorifics. No absent says verb is inserted after pulpit.

The historical second account explicitly retains به after the verb; selected and modern do not. Selected: «فدعت بطيب فمست، ثم قالت». brill-1862 (PDF 322): «فدعت بطيب فمست به ثم قالت». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 310): «فدعت بطيب فمست ثم قالت».

segments.arabic: [1223] حدثنا آدم حدثنا شعبة حدثنا ثابت عن أنس بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Adam related to us: Shu‘bah related to us: Thabit related to us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: مر النبي ﷺ بامرأة تبكي عند قبر، فقال اتقي الله واصبري قالت إليك عني فإنك لم تصب بمصيبتي ولم تعرفه فقيل لها إنه النبي ﷺ فأتت باب النبي ﷺ فلم تجد عنده بوابين فقالت لم أعرفك، فقال إنما الصبر عند الصدمة الأولى
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed a woman weeping at a grave. He said, “Fear Allah and be patient.” She said, “Away from me, for you have not been afflicted with my calamity.” She did not recognize him. She was told, “He is the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” She came to the door of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and found no doorkeepers there. She said, “I did not recognize you.” He said, “Patience is only at the first shock.”

comparisons.note: The source’s she-did-not-recognize-him statement occurs after her reply and is not part of her words.

checkedBody: Narrated Anas bin Malik:

The Prophet passed by a woman who was weeping beside a grave. He told her to fear Allah and be patient. She said to him, "Go away, for you have not been afflicted with a calamity like mine." And she did not recognize him. Then she was informed that he was the Prophet . so she went to the house of the Prophet and there she did not find any guard. Then she said to him, "I did not recognize you." He said, "Verily, the patience is at the first stroke of a calamity."
comparisons.note: Retain door, plural doorkeepers and all three Prophetic honorific positions; do not replace door with house.

notes: The complete occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.
Keep the recognition note outside the woman’s quotation, the door and plural doorkeepers, all three honorifics, the apology without an added address and the complete first-shock response.

The historical main text lacks the selected and modern narrator note that she did not recognize him. Selected: «فإنك لم تصب بمصيبتي ولم تعرفه فقيل لها». brill-1862 (PDF 323): «فإنك لم تصب بمصيبتي فقيل لها». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 310): «فإنك لم تصب بمصيبتي ولم تعرفه فقيل لها».

segments.arabic: [1224] حدثنا عبدان ومحمد قالا: أخبرنا عبد الله أخبرنا عاصم بن سليمان عن أبي عثمان قال: حدثني أسامة بن زيد رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: ‘Abdan and Muhammad related to us; they said: ‘Abd Allah informed us: ‘Asim ibn Sulayman informed us, from Abu ‘Uthman, who said: Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, related to me; he said:

segments.arabic: أرسلت ابنة النبي ﷺ إليه إن ابنا لي قبض فائتنا فأرسل يقريء السلام ويقول إن لله ما أخذ وله ما أعطى وكل عنده بأجل مسمى فلتصبر ولتحتسب فأرسلت إليه تقسم عليه ليأتينها فقام ومعه سعد بن عبادة ومعاذ بن جبل وأبي بن كعب وزيد بن ثابت ورجال فرفع إلى رسول الله ﷺ الصبي ونفسه تتقعقع
segments.english: The daughter of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent to him: “A son of mine is dying, so come to us.” He sent greetings of peace and said, “To Allah belongs what He takes, and to Him belongs what He gives. Everything with Him has an appointed term, so let her be patient and seek reward.” She sent to him, adjuring him to come to her. He rose, accompanied by Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, Mu‘adh ibn Jabal, Ubayy ibn Ka‘b, Zayd ibn Thabit, and men. The boy was lifted up to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with his breath rattling.

segments.arabic: قال حسبته أنه قال: كانها شن
segments.english: He said: I think he said, “As though it were a worn waterskin.”

segments.arabic: ففاضت عيناه، فقال سعد يا رسول الله ما هذا، فقال هذه رحمة جعلها الله في قلوب عباده وإنما يرحم الله من عباده الرحماء
segments.english: His eyes overflowed. Sa‘d said, “Messenger of Allah, what is this?” He said, “This is mercy that Allah has placed in the hearts of His servants. And Allah has mercy only on the merciful among His servants.”

comparisons.note: Drops the narrator’s uncertainty before the waterskin comparison and supplies an explicit Usama attribution. The bracketed identification of the daughter is external commentary. The selected breath-rattling description, second Prophetic honorific and restrictive only in the mercy saying must remain.

checkedBody: Narrated Usama bin Zaid:

The daughter of the Prophet (p.b.u.h) sent (a messenger) to the Prophet requesting him to come as her child was dying (or was gasping), but the Prophet returned the messenger and told him to convey his greeting to her and say: "Whatever Allah takes is for Him and whatever He gives, is for Him, and everything with Him has a limited fixed term (in this world) and so she should be patient and hope for Allah's reward." She again sent for him, swearing that he should come. The Prophet got up, and so did Sad bin 'Ubada, Muadh bin Jabal, Ubai bin Ka'b, Zaid bin Thabit and some other men. The child was brought to Allah's Apostle while his breath was disturbed in his chest (the sub-narrator thinks that Usama added: ) as if it was a leather water-skin. On that the eyes of the Prophet (p.b.u.h) started shedding tears. Sad said, "O Allah's Apostle! What is this?" He replied, "It is mercy which Allah has lodged in the hearts of His slaves, and Allah is merciful only to those of His slaves who are merciful (to others).
comparisons.note: Adds explanatory parentheses outside the selected wording; the narrator uncertainty and breath comparison need exact role review.

notes: The uncertainty about the waterskin comparison belongs to the transmission, not an unqualified direct quotation.

Keep the named companions, both Prophetic honorifics, greetings, appointed term, breath-rattling, I-think qualification and restrictive only. Dying follows the classical explanation of the approaching-death expression; do not import a daughter or child identity.

The historical closing connector differs from selected and modern. Selected: «وإنما يرحم الله من عباده الرحماء». brill-1862 (PDF 323): «فإنما يرحم الله من عباده الرحماء». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 310): «وإنما يرحم الله من عباده الرحماء».

The historical wording uses بنت, while selected and modern use ابنة. Both refer to daughter; no identity is inserted. Selected: «أرسلت ابنة النبي». brill-1862 (PDF 323): «أرسلت بنت النبي». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 310): «أرسلت ابنة النبي».

segments.arabic: [1225] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد حدثنا أبو عامر حدثنا فليح بن سليمان عن هلال بن علي عن أنس بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us: Abu ‘Amir related to us: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from Hilal ibn ‘Ali, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: شهدنا بنتا لرسول الله ﷺ قال: ورسول الله ﷺ جالس على القبر قال: فرأيت عينيه تدمعان قال، فقال هل منكم رجل لم يقارف الليلة، فقال أبو طلحة أنا قال: فانزل قال: فنزل في قبرها
segments.english: We attended a daughter of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sitting by the grave. He said: I saw his eyes shedding tears. He said: Then he asked, “Is there a man among you who did not have intercourse last night?” Abu Talhah said, “I.” He said, “Then go down.” He said: He went down into her grave.

comparisons.note: The bracketed identification of the daughter is external commentary, and the chosen explanation of يقارف requires separate lexical review.

checkedBody: Narrated Anas bin Malik:

We were (in the funeral procession) of one of the daughters of the Prophet and he was sitting by the side of the grave. I saw his eyes shedding tears. He said, "Is there anyone among you who did not have sexual relations with his wife last night?" Abu Talha replied in the affirmative. And so the Prophet told him to get down in the grave. And so he got down in her grave.
comparisons.note: Adds with his wife to the selected يقارف wording and chooses a lexical interpretation; do not copy the explanatory addition into the source translation. Keep the explicit I reply and all source reporting introductions, rather than only saying that Abu Talhah replied affirmatively.

notes: The complete occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.

The selected qiraf word is rendered intercourse without adding with-his-wife or naming the daughter. Classical commentary also records a sin-related reading; this lexical alternative remains in source notes, not silently erased. Keep all reporting introductions and the brief descent command.

The historical opening names the Prophet; selected and modern name the Messenger of Allah. Selected: «بنتا لرسول الله ﷺ». brill-1862 (PDF 324): «بنتا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 311): «بنتا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم».

The historical command includes into-her-grave before the separately reported descent. The selected command remains Then go down, followed by the full descent account. Selected: «قال: فانزل قال: فنزل في قبرها». brill-1862 (PDF 324): «قال فانزل في قبرها قال فنزل في قبرها». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 311): «قال فانزل قال فنزل في قبرها».

segments.arabic: [1226] حدثنا عبدان حدثنا عبد الله أخبرنا ابن جريج قال: أخبرني عبد الله بن عبيد الله بن أبي مليكة قال
segments.english: ‘Abdan related to us: ‘Abd Allah related to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us; he said: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me; he said:

segments.arabic: توفيت ابنة لعثمان رضى الله تعالى عنه بمكة وجئنا لنشهدها وحضرها بن عمر وابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهم وإني لجالس بينهما
segments.english: A daughter of ‘Uthman, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, died in Makkah, and we came to attend her. Ibn ‘Umar and Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, were present, and I was sitting between them.

segments.arabic: أو قال جلست إلى أحدهما ثم جاء الآخر فجلس إلى جنبي،
segments.english: Or he said: “I sat beside one of them, then the other came and sat beside me.”

segments.arabic: فقال عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما لعمرو بن عثمان ألا تنهى عن البكاء فأن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إن الميت ليعذب ببكاء أهله عليه،
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said to ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman, “Will you not forbid the weeping? For the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘The deceased is indeed punished because of his family’s weeping over him.’”

segments.arabic: فقال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قد كان عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه يقول بعض ذلك ثم حدث قال صدرت مع عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه من مكة حتى إذا كنا بالبيداء إذا هو بركب تحت ظل سمرة، فقال اذهب فانظر من هؤلاء الركب قال: فنظرت فإذا صهيب فأخبرته، فقال ادعه لي فرجعت إلى صهيب فقلت: ارتحل فالحق أمير المؤمنين فلما أصيب عمر دخل صهيب يبكي يقول وا أخاه وا صاحباه، فقال عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه يا صهيب أتبكي علي وقد قال رسول الله ﷺ: إن الميت يعذب ببعض بكاء أهله عليه
segments.english: Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said, “‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, used to say some of that.” Then he related, saying: “I departed from Makkah with ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. When we were at al-Bayda’, there was a party of riders in the shade of a samurah tree. He said, ‘Go and see who these riders are.’” He said: “I looked, and there was Suhayb. I informed him, and he said, ‘Call him to me.’ I returned to Suhayb and said, ‘Set out and join the Commander of the Believers.’ When ‘Umar was struck, Suhayb entered weeping, saying, ‘Alas, my brother! Alas, my companion!’ ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said, ‘Suhayb, are you weeping over me when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has said, “The deceased is punished because of some of his family’s weeping over him”?’”

segments.arabic: قال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما فلما مات عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه ذكرت ذلك لعائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها فقالت رحم الله عمر والله ما حدث رسول الله ﷺ إن الله ليعذب المؤمن ببكاء أهله عليه ولكن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إن الله ليزيد الكافر عذابا ببكاء أهله عليه وقالت حسبكم القرآن { ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى }
segments.english: Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said: When ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, died, I mentioned that to ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her. She said, “May Allah have mercy on ‘Umar. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not state that Allah punishes the believer because of his family’s weeping over him. Rather, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Allah indeed increases the disbeliever’s punishment because of his family’s weeping over him.’” She said, “The Qur’an is sufficient for you: ‘No bearer of a burden bears the burden of another.’”

segments.arabic: قال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما عند ذلك والله { هو أضحك وأبكى }
segments.english: Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said at that point, “By Allah, ‘He makes laugh and makes weep.’”

segments.arabic: قال ابن أبي مليكة والله ما قال ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما شيئا
segments.english: Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: By Allah, Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said nothing.

comparisons.note: Omits the qualifier بعض in Ibn Abbas’s initial statement about Umar; keep the three embedded accounts and every attribution distinct. Preserve all twelve companion honorifics, both narrator oaths, the explicit some-of-that qualification and the source’s complete attributions.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Abdullah bin 'Ubaidullah bin Abi Mulaika:

One of the daughters of 'Uthman died at Mecca. We went to attend her funeral procession. Ibn 'Umar and Ibn Abbas were also present. I sat in between them (or said, I sat beside one of them. Then a man came and sat beside me.) 'Abdullah bin 'Umar said to 'Amr bin 'Uthman, "Will you not prohibit crying as Allah's Apostle has said, 'The dead person is tortured by the crying of his relatives.?" Ibn Abbas said, "Umar used to say so." Then he added narrating, "I accompanied Umar on a journey from Mecca till we reached Al-Baida. There he saw some travelers in the shade of a Samura (A kind of forest tree). He said (to me), "Go and see who those travelers are." So I went and saw that one of them was Suhaib. I told this to 'Umar who then asked me to call him. So I went back to Suhaib and said to him, "Depart and follow the chief of the faithful believers." Later, when 'Umar was stabbed, Suhaib came in weeping and saying, "O my brother, O my friend!" (on this 'Umar said to him, "O Suhaib! Are you weeping for me while the Prophet said, "The dead person is punished by some of the weeping of his relatives?" Ibn Abbas added, "When 'Umar died I told all this to Aisha and she said, 'May Allah be merciful to Umar. By Allah, Allah's Apostle did not say that a believer is punished by the weeping of his relatives. But he said, Allah increases the punishment of a non-believer because of the weeping of his relatives." Aisha further added, "The Quran is sufficient for you (to clear up this point) as Allah has stated: 'No burdened soul will bear another's burden.' " (35.18). Ibn Abbas then said, "Only Allah makes one laugh or cry." Ibn Umar did not say anything after that.

segments.arabic: [1227] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف أخبرنا مالك عن عبد الله بن أبي بكر عن أبيه عن عمرة بنت عبد الرحمن أنها أخبرته أنها سمعت عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها زوج النبي ﷺ قالت

segments.arabic: إنما مر رسول الله ﷺ على يهودية يبكي عليها أهلها، فقال إنهم ليبكون عليها وإنها لتعذب في قبرها
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had only passed a Jewish woman whose family were weeping over her. He said, “They are indeed weeping over her, while she is being punished in her grave.”

segments.arabic: سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: إن كذبا علي ليس ككذب على أحد من كذب علي متعمدا فليتبوأ مقعده من النار سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: من نيح عليه يعذب بما نيح عليه
segments.english: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, “A lie about me is not like a lie about anyone else. Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.” I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, “Whoever is wailed over is punished because of the wailing over him.”

segments.arabic: [1231] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله حدثنا سفيان حدثنا ابن المنكدر قال: سمعت جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us: Sufyan related to us: Ibn al-Munkadir related to us; he said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, say:

segments.arabic: جيء بأبي يوم أحد قد مثل به حتى وضع بين يدي رسول الله ﷺ وقد سجي ثوبا فذهبت أريد أن أكشف عنه فنهاني قومي ثم ذهبت أكشف عنه فنهاني قومي فأمر رسول الله ﷺ فرفع فسمع صوت صائحة، فقال من هذه فقالوا ابنة عمرو أو أخت عمرو قال: فلم تبكي أو لا تبكي فما زالت الملائكة تظله بأجنحتها حتى رفع
segments.english: My father was brought on the day of Uhud, having been mutilated, and was placed before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, covered with a cloth. I went, intending to uncover him, but my people forbade me. Then I went to uncover him, but my people forbade me. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave an order, and he was lifted away. He heard the voice of a woman crying out and said, “Who is this?” They said, “The daughter of ‘Amr—or the sister of ‘Amr.” He said, “Why is she weeping?”—or, “Let her not weep.”—“The angels continued to shade him with their wings until he was lifted away.”

comparisons.note: Keep both Prophetic honorifics, both daughter/sister alternatives and both question/prohibition alternatives.

checkedBody: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah :

On the day of the Battle of Uhud, my father was brought and he had been mayhemed and was placed in front of Allah's Apostle and a sheet was over him. I went intending to uncover my father but my people forbade me; again I wanted to uncover him but my people forbade me. Allah's Apostle gave his order and he was shifted away. At that time he heard the voice of a crying woman and asked, "Who is this?" They said, "It is the daughter or the sister of Amr." He said, "Why does she weep? (or let her stop weeping), for the angels had been shading him with their wings till he (i.e. the body of the martyr) was shifted away."
comparisons.note: Retain the second complete uncovering action, both alternatives and both honorifics without an added martyr description.

segments.arabic: [1233] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن عامر بن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن أبيه رضى الله تعالى عنه قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Amir ibn Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ يعودني عام حجة الوداع من وجع اشتد بي فقلت: إني قد بلغ بي من الوجع وأنا ذو مال ولا يرثني إلا ابنة أفأتصدق بثلثي مالي قال لا فقلت: بالشطر، فقال لا، ثم قال الثلث والثلث كبير أو كثير إنك أن تذر ورثتك أغنياء خير من أن تذرهم عالة يتكففون الناس وإنك لن تنفق نفقة تبتغي بها وجه الله إلا أجرت بها حتى ما تجعل في في امرأتك فقلت: يا رسول الله أخلف بعد أصحابي قال إنك لن تخلف فتعمل عملا صالحا إلا ازددت به درجة ورفعة ثم لعلك أن تخلف حتى ينتفع بك أقوام ويضر بك آخرون اللهم أمض لأصحابي هجرتهم ولا تردهم على أعقابهم لكن البائس سعد بن خولة
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to visit me in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage because of an illness that had become severe. I said, “The illness has brought me to this state. I have wealth, and only a daughter inherits from me. Shall I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity?” He said, “No.” I said, “Half?” He said, “No.” Then he said, “A third, and a third is great—or much. To leave your heirs wealthy is better than to leave them dependent, begging from people. You will not spend anything seeking thereby the Face of Allah without being rewarded for it, even what you put into your wife’s mouth.” I said, “Messenger of Allah, will I be left behind after my companions?” He said, “You will not be left behind and do a righteous deed without thereby increasing in degree and elevation. Then perhaps you will be left behind, so that some people benefit through you and others are harmed through you. Allah, complete my companions’ emigration for them, and do not turn them back on their heels. But poor Sa‘d ibn Khawlah!”

segments.arabic: يرثى له رسول الله ﷺ أن مات بمكة
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, grieved for him because he died in Makkah.

comparisons.note: The rendering of لن تخلف risks an unconditional assertion that he will not be left behind; check the full conditional construction against the Arabic before translation. Preserve Messenger of Allah rather than replacing it with Prophet, and what-you-put without importing a morsel noun. The final grief explanation remains a narrator comment.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Amir bin Sad bin Abi Waqqas:

That his father said, "In the year of the last Hajj of the Prophet I became seriously ill and the Prophet used to visit me inquiring about my health. I told him, 'I am reduced to this state because of illness and I am wealthy and have no inheritors except a daughter, (In this narration the name of 'Amir bin Sad is mentioned and in fact it is a mistake; the narrator is 'Aisha bint Sad bin Abi Waqqas). Should I give two-thirds of my property in charity?' He said, 'No.' I asked, 'Half?' He said, 'No.' then he added, 'One-third, and even one-third is much. You'd better leave your inheritors wealthy rather than leaving them poor, begging others. You will get a reward for whatever you spend for Allah's sake, even for what you put in your wife's mouth.' I said, 'O Allah's Apostle! Will I be left alone after my companions have gone?' He said, 'If you are left behind, whatever good deeds you will do will up-grade you and raise you high. And perhaps you will have a long life so that some people will be benefited by you while others will be harmed by you. O Allah! Complete the emigration of my companions and do not turn them renegades.' But Allah's Apostle felt sorry for poor Sad bin Khaula as he died in Mecca." (but Sad bin Abi Waqqas lived long after the Prophet (p.b.u.h).)

segments.arabic: [1234] وقال الحكم بن موسى حدثنا يحيى بن حمزة عن عبد الرحمن بن جابر أن القاسم بن مخيمرة حدثه قال: حدثني أبو بردة بن أبي موسى رضى الله تعالى عنه قال

segments.english: Abu Musa fell ill and fainted, with his head in the lap of a woman of his family, and he could not respond to her at all. When he recovered consciousness, he said, “I am free of those from whom the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, declared himself free. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, declared himself free of the woman who wails, the woman who shaves her hair, and the woman who tears her clothes.”

segments.arabic: [1237] حدثنا محمد بن المثنى حدثنا عبد الوهاب قال: سمعت يحيى قال: أخبرتني عمرة قالت سمعت عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت

segments.arabic: لما جاء النبي ﷺ قتل بن حارثة وجعفر وابن رواحة جلس يعرف فيه الحزن وأنا أنظر من صائر الباب
segments.english: When news of the killing of Ibn Harithah, Ja‘far and Ibn Rawahah reached the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he sat down with grief apparent in him, while I was looking through the opening of the door.

segments.arabic: شق الباب
segments.english: The crack in the door.

segments.arabic: فأتاه رجل، فقال إن نساء جعفر وذكر بكاءهن فأمره أن ينهاهن فذهب ثم أتاه الثانية لم يطعنه، فقال انههن فأتاه الثالثة قال والله غلبننا يا رسول الله
segments.english: A man came to him and said, “The women of Ja‘far”—and he mentioned their weeping. He ordered him to forbid them. He went, then came to him a second time; they had not obeyed him. He said, “Forbid them.” He came to him a third time and said, “By Allah, they have overcome us, Messenger of Allah.”

segments.arabic: فزعمت أنه قال:
segments.english: She stated that he said:

segments.arabic: فاحث في أفواههن التراب فقلت: أرغم الله أنفك لم تفعل ما أمرك رسول الله ﷺ ولم تترك رسول الله ﷺ من العناء
segments.english: “Then cast dust into their mouths.” I said, “May Allah rub your nose in the dust! You did not do what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded you, and you did not spare the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the trouble.”

comparisons.note: Drops ibn from Ibn Harithah, naming Harithah instead. The door-opening gloss and each reporting attribution require separate role review.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Aisha:

When the Prophet got the news of the death of Ibn Haritha, Ja'far and Ibn Rawaha he sat down and looked sad and I was looking at him through the chink of the door. A man came and told him about the crying of the women of Ja'far. The Prophet ordered him to forbid them. The man went and came back saying that he had told them but they did not listen to him. The Prophet (p.b.u.h) said, "Forbid them." So again he went and came back for the third time and said, "O Allah's Apostle! By Allah, they did not listen to us at all." ('Aisha added): Allah's Apostle ordered him to go and put dust in their mouths. I said, (to that man) "May Allah stick your nose in the dust (i.e. humiliate you)! You could neither (persuade the women to) fulfill the order of Allah's Apostle nor did you relieve Allah's Apostle from fatigue. "
comparisons.note: Adds explanatory parentheses and does not retain the selected reporting qualification فزعمت as such.

segments.arabic: [1239] حدثنا بشر بن الحكم حدثنا سفيان بن عيينة أخبرنا إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة أنه سمع أنس بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه يقول

segments.arabic: اشتكى بن لأبي طلحة قال: فمات وأبو طلحة خارج فلما رأت امرأته أنه قد مات هيأت شيئا ونحته في جانب البيت فلما جاء أبو طلحة قال كيف الغلام قالت قد هدأت نفسه وأرجو أن يكون قد استراح وظن أبو طلحة أنها صادقة قال: فبات فلما أصبح اغتسل فلما أراد أن يخرج أعلمته أنه قد مات فصلى مع النبي ﷺ ثم أخبر النبي ﷺ بما كان منهما، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: لعل الله أن يبارك لكما في ليلتكما
segments.english: A son of Abu Talhah fell ill. He said: He died while Abu Talhah was away. When his wife saw that he had died, she prepared something and moved him to the side of the house. When Abu Talhah came, he asked, “How is the boy?” She said, “His soul has become still, and I hope he has found rest.” Abu Talhah thought that she was telling the truth. He said: He spent the night. When morning came, he bathed. When he intended to leave, she informed him that the boy had died. He prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then informed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, of what had happened between them. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Perhaps Allah will bless you both in your night.”

segments.arabic: قال سفيان، فقال رجل من الأنصار فرأيت لهما تسعة أولاد كلهم قد قرأ القرآن
segments.english: Sufyan said: A man of the Ansar then said, “I saw that they had nine children, all of whom had recited the Qur’an.”

comparisons.note: Renders فرأيت as I think rather than preserving its seeing/reporting form. The original locator also captured the following differently punctuated chapter heading and its context; the revised locator separates that material.

checkedBody: Narrated Anas bin Malik:

One of the sons of Abu Talha became sick and died and Abu Talha at that time was not at home. When his wife saw that he was dead, she prepared him (washed and shrouded him) and placed him somewhere in the house. When Abu Talha came, he asked, "How is the boy?" She said, "The child is quiet and I hope he is in peace." Abu Talha thought that she had spoken the truth. Abu Talha passed the night and in the morning took a bath and when he intended to go out, she told him that his son had died, Abu Talha offered the (morning) prayer with the Prophet and informed the Prophet of what happened to them. Allah's Apostle said, "May Allah bless you concerning your night. (That is, may Allah bless you with good offspring)." Sufyan said, "One of the Ansar said, 'They (i.e. Abu Talha and his wife) had nine sons and all of them became reciters of the Quran (by heart).' "
comparisons.note: Adds washing/shrouding, morning, offspring and memorization explanations; changes the selected لعل صيغة and omits the closing seeing/reporting form.

segments.arabic: [1241] حدثنا الحسن بن عبد العزيز حدثنا يحيى بن حسان حدثنا قريش هو ابن حيان عن ثابت عن أنس بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Al-Hasan ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us: Yahya ibn Hassan related to us: Quraysh—he is Ibn Hayyan—related to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: دخلنا مع رسول الله ﷺ على أبي سيف القين وكان ظئرا لإبراهيم عليه السلام فأخذ رسول الله ﷺ إبراهيم فقبله وشمه ثم دخلنا عليه بعد ذلك وإبراهيم يجود بنفسه فجعلت عينا رسول الله ﷺ تذرفان، فقال له عبد الرحمن بن عوف رضى الله تعالى عنه وأنت يا رسول الله، فقال: يا ابن عوف إنها رحمة ثم أتبعها بأخرى، فقال ﷺ إن العين تدمع والقلب يحزن ولا نقول إلا ما يرضى ربنا وإنا بفراقك يا إبراهيم لمحزونون
segments.english: We entered with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, upon Abu Sayf the blacksmith, who was the foster father of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took Ibrahim, kissed him and smelled him. Then we entered upon him after that, while Ibrahim was breathing his last. The eyes of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, began to shed tears. ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said to him, “Even you, Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Ibn ‘Awf, this is mercy.” Then he followed it with another, and said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “The eye sheds tears and the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. And we are indeed grieved by your departure, Ibrahim.”

segments.arabic: رواه موسى عن سليمان بن المغيرة عن ثابت عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Musa narrated it from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

comparisons.note: Calls Abu Sayf the father of Ibrahim’s wet-nurse, while the Khan comparison calls him her husband. The selected ظئرا needs explicit lexical review. The closing route omits Musa and Thabit, and the original locator includes the following unpunctuated chapter heading; the revised locator separates it. Classical commentary identifies ظئر as foster father, the husband of the wet-nurse, not her father. It also records another tear or another utterance for ثم أتبعها بأخرى; this working translation leaves the unspecified noun unfilled.

checkedBody: Narrated Anas bin Malik:

We went with Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) to the blacksmith Abu Saif, and he was the husband of the wet-nurse of Ibrahim (the son of the Prophet). Allah's Apostle took Ibrahim and kissed him and smelled him and later we entered Abu Saif's house and at that time Ibrahim was in his last breaths, and the eyes of Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) started shedding tears. 'Abdur Rahman bin 'Auf said, "O Allah's Apostle, even you are weeping!" He said, "O Ibn 'Auf, this is mercy." Then he wept more and said, "The eyes are shedding tears and the heart is grieved, and we will not say except what pleases our Lord, O Ibrahim ! Indeed we are grieved by your separation."
comparisons.note: Omits the full closing Musa/Sulayman/Thabit/Anas route and adds explanatory identification. The exact ظئر relationship needs lexical review. Do not supply weeping in the question or more tears in the unspecified then-he-followed-it-with-another phrase. Keep Ibrahim’s honorific, every Prophetic honorific and the complete closing route.

notes: Keep Ibrahim’s honorific, the complete closing corroborating route, and the lexical relationship review separate. The next web chapter heading is now excluded from this body.

Foster father follows the classical husband-of-wet-nurse explanation, not father-of-wet-nurse. Another is unspecified: commentary records a tear or utterance, so neither noun is inserted. Retain all five Prophetic honorifics, Ibrahim’s honorific and the complete Musa/Sulayman/Thabit/Anas closing route.

segments.arabic: [1242] حدثنا أصبغ عن ابن وهب قال: أخبرني عمرو عن سعيد بن الحارث الأنصارى عن عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Asbagh related to us, from Ibn Wahb, who said: ‘Amr informed me, from Sa‘id ibn al-Harith al-Ansari, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: اشتكى سعد بن عبادة شكوى له فأتاه النبي ﷺ يعوده مع عبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد بن أبي وقاص وعبد الله بن مسعود رضى الله تعالى عنهم فلما دخل عليه فوجده في غاشية أهله، فقال قد قضى قالوا لا يا رسول الله فبكى النبي ﷺ فلما رأى القوم بكاء النبي ﷺ بكوا، فقال ألا تسمعون إن الله لا يعذب بدمع العين ولا بحزن القلب ولكن يعذب بهذا
segments.english: Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah fell ill with an illness of his. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to visit him with ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas and ‘Abd Allah ibn Mas‘ud, may Allah Most High be pleased with them. When he entered upon him and found him surrounded by his family, he asked, “Has he passed away?” They said, “No, Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wept. When the people saw the weeping of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, they wept. He said, “Do you not hear? Allah does not punish because of the eye’s tears or the heart’s grief, but He punishes because of this”—

segments.arabic: وأشار إلى لسانه
segments.english: and he pointed to his tongue—

segments.arabic: أو يرحم وإن الميت يعذب ببكاء أهله عليه
segments.english: “or shows mercy. And the deceased is indeed punished because of his family’s weeping over him.”

segments.arabic: وكان عمر رضي الله عنه يضرب فيه بالعصا ويرمي بالحجارة ويحثي بالتراب
segments.english: And ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to strike with a stick because of it, throw stones, and scatter dust.

comparisons.note: Contains the final Umar statement present in both prints but absent from the selected Arabic; it cannot be silently appended to this source translation.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Abdullah bin 'Umar :

Sad bin 'Ubada became sick and the Prophet along with 'Abdur Rahman bin 'Auf, Sad bin Abi Waqqas and 'Abdullah bin Masud visited him to enquire about his health. When he came to him, he found him surrounded by his household and he asked, "Has he died?" They said, "No, O Allah's Apostle." The Prophet wept and when the people saw the weeping of Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) they all wept. He said, "Will you listen? Allah does not punish for shedding tears, nor for the grief of the heart but he punishes or bestows His Mercy because of this." He pointed to his tongue and added, "The deceased is punished for the wailing of his relatives over him." 'Umar used to beat with a stick and throw stones and put dust over the faces (of those who used to wail over the dead).
comparisons.note: Contains the Umar closing statement absent from the selected Arabic and adds an explanatory parenthesis about the people concerned. The selected بكاء is weeping, not wailing. The printed supplement does not explicitly say faces or add an object identifying people who wail.

notes: Both Arabic prints and both English comparisons contain an Umar closing statement absent from the selected source. Record the omission; do not silently append it.

segments.arabic: [1243] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله بن حوشب حدثنا عبد الوهاب حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد قال: أخبرتني عمرة قالت سمعت عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها تقول
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hawshab related to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us; he said: ‘Amrah informed me; she said: I heard ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, say:

segments.arabic: لما جاء قتل زيد بن حارثة وجعفر وعبد الله بن رواحة جلس النبي ﷺ يعرف فيه الحزن وأنا أطلع من شق الباب فأتاه رجل، فقال: يا رسول الله إن نساء جعفر وذكر بكاءهن فأمره بأن ينهاهن فذهب الرجل ثم أتى، فقال قد نهيتهن وذكر أنهن لم يطعنه فأمره الثانية أن ينهاهن فذهب ثم أتى، فقال والله لقد غلبنني أو غلبننا
segments.english: When news of the killing of Zayd ibn Harithah, Ja‘far and ‘Abd Allah ibn Rawahah came, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat down with grief apparent in him, while I was looking through the crack in the door. A man came to him and said, “Messenger of Allah, the women of Ja‘far”—and he mentioned their weeping. He ordered him to forbid them. The man went, then came and said, “I have forbidden them,” and mentioned that they had not obeyed him. He ordered him a second time to forbid them. He went, then came and said, “By Allah, they have indeed overcome me—or overcome us.”

segments.arabic: الشك من محمد بن حوشب
segments.english: The uncertainty is from Muhammad ibn Hawshab.

segments.arabic: فزعمت أن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: She stated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: فاحث في أفواههن التراب فقلت: أرغم الله أنفك فوالله ما أنت بفاعل وما تركت رسول الله ﷺ من العناء
segments.english: “Then cast dust into their mouths.” I said, “May Allah rub your nose in the dust! By Allah, you are not going to do it, and you have not spared the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the trouble.”

comparisons.note: Drops Zayd ibn from Zayd ibn Harithah and omits the opening address to the Messenger. Preserve the named transmitter’s me/us uncertainty and every attribution. Keep the oath, future-facing you-are-not-going-to-do-it wording, all honorifics, and the separate Amrah/Aishah attribution without implying doubt.

checkedBody: Narrated Aisha:

When the news of the martyrdom of Zaid bin Haritha, Ja'far and 'Abdullah bin Rawaha came, the Prophet sat down looking sad, and I was looking through the chink of the door. A man came and said, "O Allah's Apostle! The women of Ja'far," and then he mentioned their crying . The Prophet (p.b.u.h) ordered h im to stop them from crying. The man went and came back and said, "I tried to stop them but they disobeyed." The Prophet (p.b.u.h) ordered him for the second time to forbid them. He went again and came back and said, "They did not listen to me, (or "us": the sub-narrator Muhammad bin Haushab is in doubt as to which is right). " ('Aisha added: The Prophet said, "Put dust in their mouths." I said (to that man), "May Allah stick your nose in the dust (i.e. humiliate you)." By Allah, you could not (stop the women from crying) to fulfill the order, besides you did not relieve Allah's Apostle from fatigue."
comparisons.note: Adds explanatory parentheses and does not retain the selected reporting qualification فزعمت as such. Preserve killed rather than martyrdom, both oaths, the exact me-or-us alternative, and you-are-not-going-to-do-it rather than could-not.

Keep all three visits, named figures, killed, both oaths and me-or-us uncertainty explicitly attributed to Muhammad ibn Hawshab. She stated preserves the attribution without necessarily implying doubt. Preserve the future-facing you-are-not-going-to-do-it expression.

segments.arabic: [1244] حدثنا عبد الله بن عبد الوهاب حدثنا حماد بن زيد حدثنا أيوب عن محمد عن أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
