segments.arabic: أخذ علينا النبي ﷺ عند البيعة أن لا ننوح فما وفت منا امرأة غير خمس نسوة أم سليم وأم العلاء وابنة أبي سبرة امرأة معاذ وامرأتان أو ابنة أبي سبرة وامرأة معاذ وامرأة أخرى
segments.english: At the pledge of allegiance, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bound us not to wail. None of our women fulfilled it except five women: Umm Sulaym, Umm al-‘Ala’, the daughter of Abu Sabrah—Mu‘adh’s wife—and two women—or the daughter of Abu Sabrah and the wife of Mu‘adh and another woman.

comparisons.note: Its punctuation makes the daughter of Abu Sabrah and the wife of Muadh appear as separate people in the first list, losing the apposition. Both list alternatives need careful translation. The first list identifies the daughter of Abu Sabrah as Muadh’s wife; the second explicitly joins the two names with and. Both lists remain.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Amir bin Rabi'a:,
The Prophet said, "Whenever you see a funeral procession, stand up till the procession goes ahead of you." Al-Humaidi added, "Till the coffin leaves you behind or is put down."

segments.english: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: كنا في جنازة فأخذ أبو هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه بيد مروان فجلسا قبل أن توضع فجاء أبو سعيد رضى الله تعالى عنه فأخذ بيد مروان، فقال قم فوالله لقد علم هذا أن النبي ﷺ نهانا عن ذلك، فقال أبو هريرة صدق
segments.english: We were at a funeral. Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, took Marwan’s hand, and they sat down before it was put down. Abu Sa‘id, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, came and took Marwan’s hand, saying, “Stand up. By Allah, this man certainly knows that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade us from doing that.” Abu Hurayrah said, “He spoke the truth.”

comparisons.note: Adds Abu to Said al-Maqburi in the opening attribution.

segments.arabic: [1248] حدثنا مسلم يعني ابن إبراهيم حدثنا هشام حدثنا يحيى عن أبي سلمة عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Muslim—meaning Ibn Ibrahim—related to us: Hisham related to us: Yahya related to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: إذا رأيتم الجنازة فقوموا فمن تبعها فلا يقعد حتى توضع
segments.english: “When you see the funeral procession, stand. Whoever follows it must not sit until it is put down.”

segments.arabic: [1249] حدثنا معاذ بن فضالة حدثنا هشام عن يحيى عن عبيد الله بن مقسم عن جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Miqsam, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: مرت بنا جنازة فقام لها النبي ﷺ وقمنا له فقلنا يا رسول الله إنها جنازة يهودي قال إذا رأيتم الجنازة فقوموا
segments.english: A funeral procession passed us. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood for it, and we stood because he did. We said, “Messenger of Allah, it is the funeral of a Jew.” He said, “When you see the funeral procession, stand.”

comparisons.note: Renders the standing relation as with him, while the selected له and modern به differ; preserve and review the selected form.

checkedBody: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah :

A funeral procession passed in front of us and the Prophet stood up and we too stood up. We said, 'O Allah's Apostle! This is the funeral procession of a Jew." He said, "Whenever you see a funeral procession, you should stand up."
comparisons.note: Does not explicitly retain the selected له relation in the shared standing phrase.

notes: The selected standing pronoun differs from both prints; preserve each reading explicitly for wording review.

The selected له is rendered because he did following Ibn Hajar’s explanation that it refers to standing because of the Prophet’s standing. The historical excerpt is explicitly corrected to فقمنا; the selected and modern readings remain unchanged.

segments.arabic: [1250] حدثنا آدم حدثنا شعبة حدثنا عمرو بن مرة قال: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى قال:
segments.english: Adam related to us: Shu‘bah related to us: ‘Amr ibn Murrah related to us; he said: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla say:

segments.arabic: كان سهل بن حنيف وقيس بن سعد قاعدين بالقادسية فمروا عليهما بجنازة فقاما فقيل لهما إنها من أهل الأرض
segments.english: Sahl ibn Hunayf and Qays ibn Sa‘d were sitting at al-Qadisiyyah. They passed them with a funeral procession, and the two stood. They were told, “It is one of the people of the land”—

segments.arabic: أي من أهل الذمة
segments.english: that is, one of the people of the covenant of protection—

segments.arabic: فقالا إن النبي ﷺ مرت به جنازة فقام فقيل له إنها جنازة يهودي، فقال أليست نفسا،
segments.english: and the two said, “A funeral procession passed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he stood. He was told, ‘It is the funeral of a Jew.’ He said, ‘Is it not a soul?’”

segments.arabic: وقال أبو حمزة عن الأعمش عن عمرو عن ابن أبي ليلى قال: كنت مع قيس وسهل رضى الله تعالى عنهما فقالا كنا مع النبي ﷺ،
segments.english: And Abu Hamzah said, from al-A‘mash, from ‘Amr, from Ibn Abi Layla, who said: I was with Qays and Sahl, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, and they said, “We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

segments.arabic: وقال زكريا عن الشعبي عن ابن أبي ليلى كان أبو مسعود وقيس يقومان للجنازة
segments.english: And Zakariyya said, from al-Sha‘bi, from Ibn Abi Layla: Abu Mas‘ud and Qays used to stand for the funeral procession.

comparisons.note: Retains closing statements but omits their Abu Hamzah/A’mash/Amr and Zakariyya/Sha’bi transmission routes.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Abdur Rahman bin Abi Laila:

Sahl bin Hunaif and Qais bin Sad were sitting in the city of Al-Qadisiya. A funeral procession passed in front of them and they stood up. They were told that funeral procession was of one of the inhabitants of the land i.e. of a non-believer, under the protection of Muslims. They said, "A funeral procession passed in front of the Prophet and he stood up. When he was told that it was the coffin of a Jew, he said, "Is it not a living being (soul)?"
comparisons.note: Omits both complete closing corroborating routes and their statements.

notes: One selected entry contains modern printed 1312/1313 plus full closing corroborations; the EPUB omits those endings.

segments.arabic: [1251] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله حدثنا الليث عن سعيد المقبري عن أبيه أنه سمع أبا سعيد الخدري رضى الله تعالى عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us: Al-Layth related to us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from his father, that he heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا وضعت الجنازة واحتملها الرجال على أعناقهم فإن كانت صالحة قالت قدموني وإن كانت غير صالحة قالت: يا ويلها أين يذهبون بها يسمع صوتها كل شيء إلا الإنسان ولو سمعه صعق
segments.english: “When the body is placed and men carry it on their necks, if it is righteous, it says, ‘Carry me forward.’ If it is not righteous, it says, ‘Woe to it! Where are they taking it?’ Everything hears its voice except the human being. If he heard it, he would faint.”

comparisons.note: Changes the third-person wording يا ويلها أين يذهبون بها to mixed first/second-person speech; review the pronoun ownership from the selected Arabic. The historical print has second-person تذهبون while selected and modern have third-person يذهبون. The English you therefore has a printed basis, but does not reproduce this selected occurrence; it is not evidence of an unequivocal error.

checkedBody: Narrated Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri :

Allah's Apostle said, When the funeral is ready and the men carry it on their shoulders, if the deceased was righteous it will say, 'Present me (hurriedly),' and if he was not righteous, it will say, 'Woe to it (me)! Where are they taking it (me)?' Its voice is heard by everything except man and if he heard it he would fall unconscious."
comparisons.note: Adds hurriedly and explanatory pronoun parentheses beyond the selected wording.

segments.arabic: [1252] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله حدثنا سفيان قال حفظناه من الزهري عن سعيد بن المسيب عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us: Sufyan related to us; he said: We memorized it from al-Zuhri, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: أسرعوا بالجنازة فإن تك صالحة فخير تقدمونها وإن يك سوى ذلك فشر تضعونه عن رقابكم
segments.english: “Carry the funeral quickly. If it is righteous, then it is a good thing you are bringing forward. If it is otherwise, then it is an evil thing you are taking off your necks.”

comparisons.note: Supplies an endpoint in the good-outcome clause although the selected occurrence lacks the modern print’s إليه.

checkedBody: Narrated Abu Huraira:
The Prophet said, "Hurry up with the dead body for if it was righteous, you are forwarding it to welfare; and if it was otherwise, then you are putting off an evil thing down your necks."
comparisons.note: Supplies an endpoint in the good-outcome clause absent from selected text; the modern print separately has إليه. The endpoint reading is supported by the modern print and by classical elliptical analyses. segments.arabic: [1253] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف حدثنا الليث حدثنا سعيد عن أبيه أنه سمع أبا سعيد الخدري رضى الله تعالى عنه قال: كان النبي ﷺ يقول:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: Al-Layth related to us: Sa‘id related to us, from his father, that he heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say:

segments.arabic: إذا وضعت الجنازة فاحتملها الرجال على أعناقهم فإن كانت صالحة قالت قدموني وإن كانت غير صالحة قالت لأهلها يا ويلها أين يذهبون بها يسمع صوتها كل شيء إلا الإنسان ولو سمع الإنسان لصعق
segments.english: “When the body is placed and men then carry it on their necks, if it is righteous, it says, ‘Carry me forward.’ If it is not righteous, it says to its people, ‘Woe to it! Where are they taking it?’ Everything hears its voice except the human being. If the human being heard it, he would faint.”

comparisons.note: Changes the selected third-person woe/where-they-take-it wording to mixed first/second-person speech. The historical print has second-person تذهبون while selected and modern have third-person يذهبون. Preserve this edition distinction, and retain Prophet used-to-say rather than replacing it with Messenger said.

checkedBody: Narrated Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri

The Prophet said, "When a funeral is ready and the men carry the deceased on their necks (shoulders), if it was pious then it will say, 'Present me quickly', and if it was not pious, then it will say, 'Woe to it (me), where are they taking it (me)?' And its voice is heard by everything except mankind and if he heard it he would fall unconscious."
comparisons.note: Omits لأهلها and adds quickly.

segments.arabic: [1256] حدثنا مسلم حدثنا شعبة حدثنا الشيباني عن الشعبي قال: أخبرني من شهد النبي ﷺ

segments.arabic: أتى على قبر منبوذ فصفهم وكبر أربعا
segments.english: He came upon a grave set apart, arranged them in rows and said the takbir four times.

segments.arabic: قلت: من حدثك قال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما
segments.english: I asked, “Who related this to you?” He said, “Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both.”

comparisons.note: The abbreviated chain makes the questioner’s role less explicit. Keep the Sha’bi/Shaybani exchange and its speaker boundaries.

checkedBody: Narrated Ash-Shaibani:

Ash Sha'bi said, "I was informed by a man who had seen the Prophet going to a grave that was separate from the other graves and he aligned the people in rows and said four Takbir." I said, "O Abu 'Amr! who narrated (that) to you"? He said, "Ibn Abbas. "
comparisons.note: Adds the Abu Amr address absent from selected text but present in the modern print.

notes: The address in the modern print and English EPUB is absent from selected and historical wording; preserve the actual questioner and respondent.

The grave-set-apart reading follows the adjective analysis recorded by al-Qastallani; he also records a foundling reading with an alternative grammatical construction. segments.arabic: [1257] حدثنا إبراهيم بن موسى أخبرنا هشام بن يوسف ان ابن جريج أخبرهم قال: أخبرني عطاء أنه سمع جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنهما يقول: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us: Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us that Ibn Jurayj informed them; he said: ‘Ata’ informed me that he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: قد توفي اليوم رجل صالح من الحبش فهلم فصلوا عليه قال: فصففنا فصلى النبي ﷺ عليه ونحن صفوف
segments.english: “A righteous man from al-Habash has died today. Come and pray over him.” He said: We formed rows, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him while we were in rows.

segments.arabic: قال أبو الزبير عن جابر كنت في الصف الثاني
segments.english: Abu al-Zubayr said, from Jabir: I was in the second row.

comparisons.note: Omits the explicit Abu al-Zubayr attribution before the closing statement about the second row. The earlier audit called this a question; it is a statement.

checkedBody: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah :

The Prophet said, "Today a pious man from Ethiopia (i.e. An Najashi) has expired, come on to offer the funeral prayer." (Jabir said): We lined up in rows and after that the Prophet led the prayer and we were in rows. Jabir added, I was in the second row."
comparisons.note: Omits the explicit Abu al-Zubayr closing attribution and supplies the Negus identification.

notes: The occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.

segments.arabic: [1258] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل حدثنا عبد الواحد حدثنا الشيباني عن عامر عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us: Al-Shaybani related to us, from ‘Amir, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ مر بقبر قد دفن ليلا، فقال متى دفن هذا قالوا البارحة قال أفلا آذنتموني قالوا دفناه في ظلمة الليل فكرهنا أن نوقظك فقام فصففنا خلفه قال ابن عباس وأنا فيهم فصلى عليه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed a grave whose occupant had been buried at night. He asked, “When was this one buried?” They said, “Last night.” He said, “Why did you not inform me?” They said, “We buried him in the darkness of the night, and we did not want to wake you.” He stood, and we formed rows behind him. Ibn ‘Abbas said: I was among them. Then he prayed over him.

comparisons.note: Renders البارحة as yesterday, losing its last-night specificity.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn Abbas:

Allah's Apostle passed by a grave of a deceased who had been buried at night. He said, "When was this (deceased) buried?" The people said, "Yesterday." He said, "Why did you not inform me?" They said, "We buried him when it was dark and so we disliked to wake you up." He stood up and we lined up behind him. (Ibn Abbas said): I was one of them, and the Prophet offered the funeral prayer.
comparisons.note: Renders البارحة as yesterday, losing last-night specificity.

notes: The occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.
Keep last night, the actual Ibn Abbas closing attribution, I-among-them and the final singular he-prayed-over-him. Do not insert an age explanation.

segments.arabic: [1259] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب حدثنا شعبة عن الشيباني عن الشعبي قال: أخبرني من مر مع نبيكم ﷺ على قبر منبوذ

segments.arabic: فأمنا فصففنا خلفه

segments.arabic: فقلنا يا أبا عمرو من حدثك قال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما
segments.english: We asked, “Abu ‘Amr, who related this to you?” He said, “Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both.”

segments.arabic: [1260] حدثنا أبو النعمان حدثنا جرير بن حازم قال: سمعت نافعا يقول
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us: Jarir ibn Hazim related to us; he said: I heard Nafi‘ say:

segments.arabic: حدث بن عمر أن أبا هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنهم يقول من تبع جنازة فله قيراط، فقال أكثر أبو هريرة علينا فصدقت
segments.english: Ibn ‘Umar was told that Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, was saying, “Whoever follows a funeral has a qirat.” He said, “Abu Hurayrah has told us a great deal.” She confirmed—

segments.arabic: يعني عائشة
segments.english: meaning ‘A’ishah—

segments.arabic: أبا هريرة وقالت سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقوله، فقال ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما لقد فرطنا في قراريط كثيرة
segments.english: Abu Hurayrah, and said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say it.” Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said, “We have indeed neglected many qirats.”

segments.arabic: فرطت ضيعت من أمر الله
segments.english: “I neglected”: “I failed in what Allah commanded.”

comparisons.note: The rendering of أكثر أبو هريرة علينا needs lexical review; the closing gloss also omits من أمر الله.

checkedBody: Narrated Nafi:

Ibn Umar was told that Abu Huraira said, "Whoever accompanies the funeral procession will have a reward equal to one Qirat." Ibn 'Umar said, "Abu Huraira talks of a too enormous reward." Aisha attested Abu Huraira's narration and said, "I heard Allah's Apostle saying like that." Ibn Umar said, "We have lost numerous Qirats."
comparisons.note: Omits the closing lexical comment فرطت ضيعت من أمر الله.

notes: Both modern printed 1323/1324 and the closing lexical gloss belong to this one selected occurrence.

Preserve passive Ibn-Umar-was-told, plural companion honorific, the separate meaning-Aishah gloss and the final lexical comment. Ibn Hajar records explanations of the much expression as quantity of narrated material or magnitude of reward; this working English uses the first without accusing fabrication. The closing gloss is a compiler lexical note, not speech by the Prophet or Ibn Umar.

segments.arabic: [1261] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة قال قرأت على بن أبي ذئب عن سعيد بن أبي سعيد المقبري عن أبيه أنه سأل أبا هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه، فقال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us; he said: I read to Ibn Abi Dhi’b, from Sa‘id ibn Abi Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from his father, that he asked Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: سمعت النبي ﷺ
segments.english: “I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

segments.arabic: حدثنا أحمد بن شبيب بن سعيد قال: حدثني أبي حدثنا يونس قال ابن شهاب وحدثني عبد الرحمن الأعرج أن أبا هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Shabib ibn Sa‘id related to us; he said: My father related to me: Yunus related to us. Ibn Shihab said: And ‘Abd al-Rahman al-A‘raj related to me that Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: من شهد الجنازة حتى يصلي فله قيراط ومن شهد حتى تدفن كان له قيراطان قيل وما القيراطان قال مثل الجبلين العظيمين
segments.english: “Whoever attends the funeral until he prays has a qirat, and whoever attends until it is buried has two qirats.” It was asked, “What are the two qirats?” He said, “Like two great mountains.”

comparisons.note: Preserves two opening report starts but abridges both selected chains. The extra historical chain is not supplied by the English body.

checkedBody: Narrated Abu Huraira:

that Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) said, "Whoever attends the funeral procession till he offers the funeral prayer for it, will get a reward equal to one Qirat, and whoever accompanies it till burial, will get a reward equal to two Qirats." It was asked, "What are two Qirats?" He replied, "Like two huge mountains."
comparisons.note: Only one introductory attribution is rendered; both complete selected opening chains must remain.

notes: Both selected opening chains must remain complete. The historical edition also has an intervening Abd Allah ibn Muhammad/Hisham/Mamar route absent from selected and modern text.

Preserve both complete selected opening chains and the first I-heard-the-Prophet account start. Selected يصلي is rendered actively; Ibn Hajar records both active and passive readings. Historical extra chain and عليه remain explicit print differences, not silent additions. Keep two great mountains without adding Uhud.

The historical main text includes a complete intervening route absent from the selected and modern main text. No chain is inserted into the selected occurrence. segments.arabic: [1262] حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم حدثنا يحيى بن أبي بكير حدثنا زائدة حدثنا أبو إسحاق الشيباني عن عامر عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال

segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to a grave. They said, “He was buried—or she was buried—last night.” Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said: We formed rows behind him. Then he prayed over her.

comparisons.note: Changes the final singular prayer actor and feminine object in ثم صلى عليها into a plural actor with masculine object.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Amir:

Ibn Abbas (who was at that time a boy) said, "Allah's Apostle came to a grave and the people said, 'He or she was buried yesterday.' " Ibn Abbas added, "We aligned behind the Prophet and he led the funeral prayer of the deceased."
comparisons.note: Adds a boy-age explanation and loses the selected feminine object pronoun in the closing prayer statement. The selected البارحة is last night, not yesterday; retain both occurrences of the companion honorific.

notes: The occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.

segments.arabic: [1263] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب عن سعيد بن المسيب وأبي سلمة أنهما حدثاه عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال

segments.arabic: نعى لنا رسول الله ﷺ النجاشي صاحب الحبشة اليوم الذي مات فيه، فقال استغفروا لأخيكم

segments.arabic: وعن ابن شهاب قال: حدثني سعيد بن المسيب أن أبا هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: And from Ibn Shihab, who said: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab related to me that Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said:

segments.arabic: إن النبي ﷺ صف بهم بالمصلى فكبر عليه أربعا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arranged them in rows at the prayer ground and said the takbir over him four times.

Allah's Apostle informed about the news of the death of An-Najash (King of Ethiopia) on the day he expired. He said, "Ask Allah's forgiveness for your brother. " Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet made them align in rows at the Musalla and said four Takbir.
comparisons.note: Omits the complete second Ibn Shihab/Said chain; keep both accounts and their separate openings.

segments.arabic: أن اليهود جاؤوا إلى النبي ﷺ برجل منهم وامرأة زنيا فأمر بهما فرجما قريبا من موضع الجنائز عند المسجد

segments.arabic: [1265] حدثنا عبيد الله بن موسى عن شيبان عن هلال هو الوزان عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, from Shayban, from Hilal—he is al-Wazzan—from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

segments.arabic: قال في مرضه الذي مات فيه لعن الله اليهود والنصارى اتخذوا قبور أنبيائهم مسجدا
segments.english: He said during the illness in which he died, “Allah cursed the Jews and the Christians. They took the graves of their prophets as a place of worship.”

segments.arabic: قالت ولولا ذلك لأبرزوا قبره غير أني أخشى أن يتخذ مسجدا
segments.english: She said: But for that, they would have made his grave prominent, but I fear that it will be taken as a place of worship.

comparisons.note: Uses plural places of worship where selected and both visually rechecked prints have singular مسجدا. The earlier historical-plural claim is explicitly corrected in this addendum; the original intake remains unchanged.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Urwa:

Aisha said, "The Prophet in his fatal illness said, 'Allah cursed the Jews and the Christians because they took the graves of their Prophets as places for praying."' Aisha added, "Had it not been for that the grave of the Prophet (p.b.u.h)
